addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

   data is known to include rows whose board intent was lost; do not present that
   bucket as proven no-board revenue.

   corrected plan. The token must remain the credential through checkout and

   required before any per-payment link is enabled.

   needs real-device testing.

   `push_subscriptions` (`shared/schema.ts:573`) has no preference column, and
   `sendPushToMerchant` is called from 13 sites with the type passed at the call
   site, never compared against anything stored. Of the design's three toggles
   only "payment received" maps to something real: there is **no daily-payout job
   at all**, and `sendPushToMerchant` is never called with a `failed` status.
   Needs: preferences column + migration `0012`, filtering inside
   `sendPushToMerchant`, a daily-payout job, and a failed-payment send site.

content.content:
- **4a Home** (`/dashboard`) — ref `dashboard.tsx`: sales revenue + chart (merchant transactions via `/api/merchants/:id/transactions`). Health strip: awaiting-payment $/count, avg sale + txn count, failed $/count — client-side aggregates of today's transactions. Recent sales list w/ method + relative time (`apple pay · 2m ago`) — fields exist on transactions. Quick actions: **new sale** → `/terminal`, **manage stock** → `/stock`, **view sales** → `/transactions`.
- **4b Stock** (`/stock`) — ref `stock-management.tsx`: product count hero; search; sort chips (a–z / price ↑ / price ↓); card grid from `/api/merchants/:id/stock-items` (icon, price, name, sold-this-week count — sold counts aggregated from transactions if that's what mobile does; else omit the subtitle); dashed **add product** card + card click → existing create/edit stock flows (desktop modal, same schemas); BEST SELLER footer computed from the same data.
- **4c Terminal** (`/terminal`) — ref `merchant-terminal-mobile-v2.tsx` (create/tap-to-pay) + `payment-stack.tsx` (active stack):
  - Left: sales revenue today + transactions today; **active stack** list with chips (all/awaiting payment/paid/failed) + search — the live payment stack (same queries/SSE updates as `payment-stack.tsx`, unlimited concurrent payments, tap row → mark paid / open detail exactly as mobile).
  - Right compose: amount (`edit>` → keypad), **paywave / boards** delivery chips, item name field (stock-item quick picks come from stock list — see tablet prototype's `custom | latte | big brunch` chips), **split bill** toggle (merchant `splitEnabled` gating — split is merchant-gated, check flag) with "customer chooses how many ways", fee line "10¢ per transaction", **send payment** → same transaction-creation mutation as mobile (`/api/transactions`), share icon → share/copy payment link (existing link from created transaction).
- **4d Analytics** (`/transactions`) — ref `transactions.tsx` + `RetailReportsButton`: totals + txn count, chart, Payment History sheet = transaction list w/ refund/receipt actions on row detail (`/api/transactions/:id/refunds`, `/receipt-pdf`), Reports/Export as per property.
- **4e Settings** — shared settings page, retail flavor (daily goal / theme if present on mobile settings stays).

## 7. Cross-cutting decisions

- **Scope dropdown** (`all properties` / `all sites` / `my store`): there is **no multi-property/site model in the schema** (single merchant scope). V1: render the dropdown as the design does with the single scope; property vertical may list distinct tenant `propertyAddress` values as filter options if trivially derivable — otherwise static single option. Do not invent a properties table.
- **Numbers animate** (count-up on hero figures), bars grow on mount (`tileIn`), report renders use `reportIn`, buttons use `popIn` where the design does. Keep all animation CSS-first (the prototype is plain CSS + tiny JS state — no animation library needed; do NOT add framer-motion etc.).
- **Fonts**: app already ships Outfit. The design also uses Plus Jakarta Sans in places — check computed styles in the design; if Jakarta appears in final screens, add the `.otf`s from `_ds/fonts` to `client/src/assets` and `@font-face` them (subset if easy); otherwise stay Outfit-only.
- **SSE**: reuse `sseClient` singleton; desktop terminal + notifications subscribe exactly like mobile pages do (beware the dual-payload/tenant-scoping fix from the 2026-07-12 audit — do not add a second parallel EventSource).

The overlay (`tutorial.tsx`) portals to `document.body`, `position: fixed`, and measures targets with `getBoundingClientRect`.

Good news: **the overlay mechanics need no changes for the scaled canvas** — `getBoundingClientRect` returns post-transform viewport coordinates, and the overlay is viewport-fixed, so the spotlight lands correctly inside the scaled/framed app. Verify this early in P0 with one dummy step.

1. **Anchors**: every desktop component that is the equivalent of a tutorial-targeted mobile control must carry the **same anchor attribute** (`data-tutorial-id="…"` / `aria-label="…"`) as its mobile counterpart. Acceptance: on desktop viewport every gated route shows an empty framed shell w/ working pill nav; phone (390px) is pixel-identical to before; tablet fills screen.
2. **P1 Retail** (default vertical): 4a → 4b → 4c → 4d. Terminal last-but-one since it's the riskiest (live payments — test with the seeded merchant, see memory `playwright-nix-chromium` for auth'd Playwright).
3. **P2 Property**: 2a → 2b → 2c → 2d.
4. **P3 Trades**: 3a → 3b → 3c → 3d.
5. **P4 Settings** (2e/3e/4e as one page) + Dashboard Preferences wiring back into Home/Analytics (`homeBigBox`, `chartStyle`, `historyStart`).
6. **P5 Tutorial adaptation** (§7a): anchors audit across all 15 screens, registry `desktopTarget/desktopBody` overrides, merged step lists where mobile pages combined into one screen, desktop-only-widget steps, mobile tutorial regression.
7. **P6 Polish + QA**: animations pass against the prototype side-by-side; health-strip drilldowns; notifications box; empty states; 402 billing-gate banner on all three terminals.

- `npm run check` (typecheck), `npx jest`, `npm run build` all green.
- Playwright screenshot matrix vs `docs/design/desktop-app/screens/`: 1440×900 (desktop, frame centered ~1000px wide, rounded, navy letterbox), 1194×834 & 1366×1024 (tablet full-bleed), 390×844 (mobile — must be unchanged; diff against pre-change screenshots).
- Functional smoke per screen with the seeded merchant (merchant 22 + minted JWT, dev server on :5000 — **single instance only**, see memory `dev-server-single-instance`): send a payment/request end-to-end, filter chips, search, sheet drag, a report generation, a settings save.

## The one that blocks the whole approach

**`printReport()` (new window + `window.print()`) will not work in your iOS app.** This is a Capacitor app (`@capacitor/ios` in `package.json`, `ios/App` present). In a WKWebView:
- `window.open('', …)` to get a writable document handle returns `null` — there are no real popup windows.
- `window.print()` is a no-op on iOS WKWebView.

So on the primary (mobile) target, "Generate PDF" would silently do nothing. Note your existing `window.open` calls (`SmartTransitions.jsx`, `merchant-url-display.tsx`) are all `mailto:`/`sms:`/external-URL — there's **no precedent that print works here**, because it doesn't. This is a "mobile-first app" whose PDF strategy only works in a desktop browser tab.

What I'd do instead: either (a) render the report HTML into an in-app route/component and use the Capacitor print/share plugin or `@capacitor/share` + a generated file, or (b) if you truly want print-to-PDF, accept it's a **desktop-web-only** feature and gate the Export button off in the native shell. Decide this before writing any of the three report files, because it changes what `printReport` even is. Worth a quick spike on one report end-to-end in the actual iOS build before committing to the pattern.

I found what exists — but there's no standalone transitions plan, so I want to confirm which thing you mean before I start. **What I searched:** `docs/`, `.agents/`, and all ~45 session transcripts (including every `ExitPlanMode` record). No transitions/motion plan doc was ever written. **What does exist:** | Source | What it covers | |---|---| | `docs/PLAN-2026-07-24-tablet-desktop-app.md:201` (§7) | The motion spec: count-up hero numbers, `tileIn` bars-grow-on-mount, `reportIn` on report render, `popIn` on buttons. Explicitly CSS-first — *"do NOT add framer-motion etc."* | | Same plan, `:230` (P6) | "animations pass against the prototype side-by-side" — the polish phase | | `docs/design/desktop-app/Taptpay Desktop.dc.html` | The authoritative prototype | | `docs/designs/motion-tablet-desktop/` | The Motion export (tablet v1/v2, desktop, landing, deck) | **Current implementation state** — the motion port is actually faithful and essentially done. The prototype defines exactly four keyframes (`tileIn`, `reportIn`, `popIn`, `glowDrift`), and `client/src/desktop/desktop.css:65-112` ports all four verbatim, wired across the retail/property/trades home, analytics, clients, terminal, stock and settings screens with staggered delays, plus a `prefers-reduced-motion` guard at `desktop.css:393`. The handoff marks P5 and P6 complete. **The one real gap I can see:** there is no page-to-page transition. `DesktopShell.tsx:105` renders `

` — clicking a nav pill swaps the screen instantly, with only the incoming page's own `popIn`/`tileIn` stagger playing. The prototype has no route transition either (it swaps by state), so this was never a port error — it'd be a deliberate addition.

On branch `feat/tablet-desktop-app`, commit `c350644` ("feat(subscription): add
plans, team logins, and billing flows", 2026-08-08) was made from a partially
staged working tree. It committed the **callers** but left their
**implementations** uncommitted in `stash@{1}`
(`wip/save-remaining-landing-and-pricing-2026-08-07`).

`npm run check` on HEAD fails with 6 errors:

- `server/routes.ts:3257` — `ReportData` still requires `currentProviderCost`,
  `ourCost`, `savings`, `currentProviderRate`, `ourRate`; routes.ts already
  stopped passing them. Fix is in the stash's `server/report-generator.ts`.
- `server/routes.ts:5175` — passes `userId` into `{ kind: "merchant" }`, which
  has no such field. Fix is the stash's widened `SseAudience`.
- `server/routes.ts:6631,6661` — call `sseBroker.disconnectUser(...)`, which does
  not exist. Fix is the stash's `SseBroker.disconnectUser` (drops live SSE
  streams for a revoked team-login principal — security-relevant to team logins).
- `server/storage.ts:1459,4436` — `platformFee` missing from
  `FinalizePaymentAttemptResult`; the stash's `server/payment-attempt-service.ts`
  edit resolves it.

Verified 2026-08-08: applying `stash@{1}` to a detached worktree at `c350644`
makes `npx tsc` exit 0. The stash's base commit **is** `c350644`, and
`git apply --check` on it passes, so it restores cleanly onto HEAD.

`stash@{2}` (`wip/save-mixed-subscription-landing-2026-08-07`, based on `7ab2b2b`)
is superseded — its subscription half became `c350644`; its landing half is
byte-identical to `stash@{1}`'s. `stash@{0}` is harness noise
(`.claude/settings.local.json` + session JSON), not real work.

Beyond the typecheck fixes, `stash@{1}` also carries the landing-page half of the
pricing repositioning — see [[landing-pricing-repositioning]] — plus Stripe
dependency removal from `package.json` and woocommerce-plugin edits. Restoring it
wholesale brings ~35 files, so review it as a unit rather than assuming it is
only landing work. Related: [[landing-phone-demo-status]].

content.text:
Now I have the full picture. Here's where things stand.

## Blocker first

`feat/tablet-desktop-app` HEAD does not typecheck — 6 errors, exactly as the `head-broken-stash1-fix` memory records. I confirmed all six live right now: `server/routes.ts:3257,5175,6631,6661` and `server/storage.ts:1459,4436`. All are server-side, and the fixes sit in `stash@{1}`.

This matters because my verify loop is `npm run check` after each phase, and I can't tell my regressions from the pre-existing six. All my work is `client/`, so it's survivable — but I'd rather not build on a red baseline.

## The three things you asked for, and why they're broken

**1. Flash on every page change — root cause found.** Each of the 15 desktop pages renders its *own* `DesktopFrame → ScaledCanvas → DesktopShell` via `DesktopPageScaffold.tsx:33-41`. So a route change unmounts and remounts the entire chrome. The killer is `ScaledCanvas.tsx:34,90`: it initialises `scale = 0` with `visibility: hidden` and only measures in a layout effect. Remounted per navigation, that blanks the whole frame for a frame — that *is* the flash you're seeing. First visit to a page adds a second flash, because the lazy chunk (`App.tsx:67-82`) hits the full-screen `PageLoader` fallback at `App.tsx:354`.

**2. The top bar moves.** `.tapt-desktop-nav` uses `justify-content: space-between`, and `.tapt-desktop-nav-item` has `padding: 0` while the active one gets `padding: 8px 22px` (`desktop.css:291-318`). The active pill is ~44px wider than its inactive self, so every other label redistributes when you change page. Plus the header remounts entirely (point 1), so the wordmark re-renders too.

**3. Pop-in exists but isn't the bounce you want.** `popIn` (`desktop.css:99`) is a single soft overshoot. The mobile app already has the real thing — `bouncePopIn` at `index.css:1022` (a proper 4-stop settle) driven by `.pt-bounce` with a `--pt-d` stagger variable. That's a proven in-repo pattern I'd reuse rather than invent.

## Plan

1. **Hoist the chrome above the router.** One persistent `DesktopFrame → ScaledCanvas → DesktopShell` mounted once in `App.tsx`; the 15 pages become plain content children. Kills the remount, the ScaledCanvas blank, and the header re-render in one move.
2. **Scope the Suspense fallback** to the page slot only, so a lazy chunk never blanks the chrome.
3. **Sliding pill bubble.** Give every nav item the active padding permanently (transparent background) so widths never change, then animate the bubble between items as a separate positioned element.
4. **Cascading bounce.** Port `bouncePopIn`/`--pt-d` into `desktop.css`, apply per-page with staggered delays keyed off the route so it replays on each navigation.
5. **Verify** — typecheck, jest, build, plus a Playwright pass at 1440×900 / 1194×834 / 1366×1024, and 390×844 to prove mobile is untouched.

Two constraints I'll hold to: mobile stays byte-identical (the shell hoist must not disturb `PageTransition`'s Switch pinning — see the `quickinv-pagetransition-fix` memory), and no animation library, per §7 of the plan.

Ready. Two things resolved while getting set up:

**Baseline is green.** Applied `stash@{1}` — `npx tsc --noEmit` now exits 0, all 6 errors gone. Caveat: that stash brings ~35 unrelated files into the working tree (landing page, pricing, woocommerce plugin, `package.json` Stripe removal). Those are *not* transitions work, so I'll keep them out of my commits and we can deal with them separately.

**The previous session left an acceptance harness.** `scripts/desktop-shots/probe-transitions.mjs` (untracked) is purpose-built for exactly this task — it instruments the DOM on every navigation and reports whether the chrome survived and whether the loader flashed, across 10 nav hops × 2 laps plus 11 pushed routes, at 1440×900 and 1194×834. Its header states the target explicitly:

> `chrome` must be `kept` on every hop … `loader` must be `no` on every hop, cold cache included.

So your "no flash reloads" requirement already has a pass/fail test. I verified its dependencies exist (`data-testid="desktop-frame"` at `DesktopFrame.tsx:26`, `DESKTOP_PRELOAD_ROUTES` at `App.tsx:112`). I'll run it first to capture the red baseline, then again after each phase.

**Order of work:**

1. Run the probe → record the "before" numbers.
2. Hoist `DesktopFrame → ScaledCanvas → DesktopShell` above the router in `App.tsx`; the 15 pages become plain content children. This is the one that kills the flash.
3. Scope the Suspense fallback to the page slot so a lazy chunk never blanks the chrome.
4. Fixed-width nav items + a separately-animated sliding bubble.
5. Port `bouncePopIn`/`--pt-d` into `desktop.css` and stagger each page's components, keyed off the route so it replays per navigation.
6. Full verify: typecheck, jest, build, probe, and a 390×844 pass proving mobile is untouched.

One thing worth flagging before I touch it: step 2 is a structural refactor across 16 files, and the desktop terminal pages carry live payment flows. I'll do it as its own commit with nothing else in it, so it's trivially revertable if the terminal misbehaves.

Say go and I'll start with the baseline probe run — I'll need the dev server on :5000, single instance only.

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(desktop): persistent chrome, sliding nav bubble, cascading entry

Tablet/desktop navigation hard-cut between screens and flashed. Two causes:
every page rendered its own DesktopFrame > ScaledCanvas > DesktopShell via
DesktopPageScaffold, and PageTransition keys a motion.div on the location with
mode="wait" — so each hop tore down the whole chrome and spent 220ms blank
before the destination mounted. ScaledCanvas starts at scale 0 / visibility
hidden until its layout effect measures, so every remount blanked the frame.

- Mount the chrome once above the router (DesktopChrome), driven by a pure
  location -> {vertical, page} map. Desktop app routes bypass PageTransition;
  mobile and public routes keep it unchanged.
- Scope the Suspense fallback to the page slot so a cold lazy chunk can no
  longer paint a full-screen loader over chrome already on screen.
- DesktopPageScaffold defers to the hoisted chrome via context, and still draws
  its own when rendered standalone, so page tests keep working.
- Nav items always carry the active padding and reserve the bold label width, so
  selecting a page cannot resize or shift them; a separate bubble slides to the
  active item.
- Add desktopBounceIn + .dt-rise/.dt-cascade and sequence every screen's entry
  blocks, so the cascade is the transition. Interaction animations (modals,

  from a generated report now replays the cascade. Accepted, easily gated.

intent: **no flash/reloads on any page change**; the **top bar must never move**
except the page-selector bubble; **every component on every page** gets a smooth
**bounce pop-in with a cascading stagger**.

all ~45 session transcripts. The motion spec is §7 (`:201`) + P6 (`:230`) of
`docs/PLAN-2026-07-24-tablet-desktop-app.md`.

Root causes (verified in code, not assumed):

1. **Flash** — every one of the 15 desktop pages renders its own
   `DesktopFrame → ScaledCanvas → DesktopShell` via `DesktopPageScaffold.tsx:33-41`,
   so a route change remounts the whole chrome. `ScaledCanvas.tsx:34,90` starts at
   `scale = 0` / `visibility: hidden` and only measures in a layout effect, so each
   remount blanks the frame for a frame. First visit adds a second flash via the
   full-screen `PageLoader` at `App.tsx:354` (lazy chunks, `App.tsx:67-82`).

   `.tapt-desktop-nav-item` has `padding: 0` while `[aria-current="page"]` gets
   `padding: 8px 22px` (`desktop.css:291-318`); the active pill is ~44px wider, so
   every sibling redistributes on each page change.
3. **Pop-in too soft** — desktop `popIn` (`desktop.css:99`) is a single overshoot.
   The real bounce already exists on mobile: `bouncePopIn` (`index.css:1022`) driven
   by `.pt-bounce` with a `--pt-d` stagger var. Reuse it; do **not** add
   framer-motion (§7 forbids it).

**Acceptance harness already written**: `scripts/desktop-shots/probe-transitions.mjs`

survived and whether the Suspense loader flashed, across 10 nav hops × 2 laps +

(see [[dev-server-single-instance]], [[playwright-nix-chromium]]).

~35 files in the tree that are **not** part of the transitions work — do not commit
them together.

Mobile must stay byte-identical; the shell hoist must not disturb
`PageTransition`'s Switch pinning ([[quickinv-pagetransition-fix]]).
